topics.title: Introduction to Chemistry and Structure of the Atom

subtopics.content: Scientific measurements, atomic structure, isotopes, electron configuration, orbitals
subtopics.objective: Master SI units, significant figures, precision, accuracy, and scientific methods; understand Dalton, Thompson, Rutherford, and Bohr atomic models; calculate relative atomic mass based on Carbon-12; write s, p, d electron configurations using Aufbau principle, Hund's rule, and Pauli exclusion principle.

topics.title: Standard Separation Techniques and Periodic Chemistry

subtopics.content: Mixture separation, periodic law, periodic trends, group/period gradations, transition elements
subtopics.objective: Classify mixtures and apply separation techniques (crystallization, distillation, chromatography); test purity using melting/boiling points; explain periodic trends (atomic radius, ionization energy, electronegativity); analyze period 3 and group 7 (halogens) chemical gradations; understand transition metal properties (variable oxidation states, complex formation, catalysis, color).

subtopics.content: Ionic, covalent, coordinate, metallic, intermolecular bonds; mole concept, chemical equations
subtopics.objective: Understand bond formation (ionic, covalent, dative, metallic) and VSEPR molecular shapes; distinguish van der Waals forces and hydrogen bonding; apply laws of chemical combination; perform mole calculations, molar concentration, empirical/molecular formula derivations, and volumetric titration stoichiometry.

topics.title: States of Matter, Energy and Energy Changes

subtopics.content: Kinetic theory, gas laws, liquids, solids, enthalpy, exothermic/endothermic processes
subtopics.objective: Apply kinetic theory to phase changes, diffusion, Brownian motion; perform calculations using gas laws (Boyle's, Charles', Graham's, Dalton's, Ideal Gas equation PV=nRT); distinguish structures of diamond and graphite; calculate enthalpy changes for combustion, neutralization, and dissolution.

subtopics.content: Arrhenius theory, pH scale, salt hydrolysis, indicators, volumetric analysis, solubility curves
subtopics.objective: Understand acid-base properties, pH calculations, and conductivity; classify salts and analyze salt hydrolysis; perform acid-base titrations; calculate solubility ($mol\,dm^{-3}$), plot solubility curves, and apply solubility rules to qualitative analysis.

topics.title: Chemical Kinetics, Equilibrium Systems and Redox

subtopics.content: Reaction rates, collision theory, Le Chatelier's principle, oxidation-reduction, electrochemical cells, electrolysis
subtopics.objective: Analyze factors affecting rates and collision/transition state theories; apply Le Chatelier's principle to dynamic equilibrium; balance redox equations; calculate standard cell e.m.f.; apply Faraday's laws of electrolysis and explain corrosion prevention.

topics.title: Chemistry of Carbon Compounds, Industry, Biochemistry and Synthetic Polymers

subtopics.content: Hydrocarbons, functional groups, isomerism, petroleum, polymers, proteins, carbohydrates, fats
subtopics.objective: Name and categorize organic functional groups (alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, alkanols, alkanoic acids, esters); understand petroleum fractional distillation and cracking; differentiate addition and condensation polymerization; analyze biochemistry of proteins, amino acids, fats/oils (saponification), and carbohydrates.

sections.sectionTitle: Section B (For candidates in Ghana only)

topics.title: Advanced Atomic Structure, Bonding, Energetics and Kinetics

subtopics.content: Mass spectrometry, nuclear chemistry, complex formation, hybridization, Hess's law, rate laws
subtopics.objective: Understand mass spectrometer operation, quantum numbers, and nuclear decay/half-life calculations; analyze complex ion geometry and bonding; master $sp, sp^2, sp^3$ hybridization and $\sigma/\pi$ bonds; apply Hess's Law, Born-Haber cycles, and bond energy calculations; calculate $K_a, K_b, pH, K_{sp}$, equilibrium constants ($K_p, K_c$), and rate law orders.

sections.sectionTitle: Section C (For candidates in Nigeria, Sierra-Leone, Liberia and The Gambia)

subtopics.content: Properties and preparations of C, O, H, N, S, Halogens, noble gases; metal extractions (Al, Fe, Sn)
subtopics.objective: Study allotropes of carbon, coal distillation, synthetic gas, and carbon oxides; examine preparations/properties of $O_2, H_2$, water hardness treatment, $Cl_2, HCl, NH_3, HNO_3, H_2SO_4$; study extraction of Aluminium, Iron, Tin, common alloys, and main compounds of Na, Ca, Cu, Fe, Al.
